Abstract: Durian fruit is one of the popular fruits in ASEAN countries, even in European countries, making it a high-potential contributor to economic growth in the agricultural sector. However, durian leaf diseases pose significant challenges in most ASEAN countries, such as Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, and Thailand. Traditionally, the identification of leaf diseases relied on manual visual inspection, a labor-intensive and tedious process. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach for durian leaf disease detection and recognition using vision transformers. We employed well-established deep learning models, VGG-19 and ResNet-9, with carefully tuned hyperparameters including epochs, optimizer, and maximum learning rate. Our results indicate that ResNet-9 achieved an impressive accuracy rate of 99.1% when using the Adam optimizer with a maximum learning rate of 0.001. This breakthrough in automated disease recognition promises to significantly reduce labor costs and time for smallholder farmers, enhancing the sustainability of durian cultivation.

Abstract: Durian cultivation in Thailand suffers substantial yield losses due to foliar diseases, yet automated detection remains challenging due to computational limitations and the need for accurate classification in real-world environments. This study proposes a transfer learning framework employing MobileNetV2, ResNet50, and EfficientNet-B0 as fixed feature extractors, combined with classical machine learning classifiers. To reduce feature dimensionality and improve efficiency, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was applied while retaining 80% of the variance. Experimental results demonstrate that Logistic Regression consistently outperforms other classifiers across all pre-trained models. Notably, the combination of EfficientNet-B0 features with Logistic Regression and PCA achieved the highest accuracy of 96.42%, an improvement from 95.23% without PCA. Detailed evaluation further revealed strong performance across disease classes, with precision, recall, and F1-scores approaching or equal to 1.00 for most categories. These findings confirm that PCA-enhanced transfer learning provides a computationally efficient and highly accurate approach for durian leaf disease classification, supporting its potential deployment in mobile and field-based agricultural systems.

Abstract: We consider high-dimensional regression over subgroups of observations. Abstract: A crucial task for a randomized controlled trial (RCT) is to specify a statistical method that can yield an efficient estimator and powerful test for the treatment effect.
